issues.text: E2K-50 of tools/test/e2e-kit.test.js is red after sub-step 1 and after sub-step 2, as the design says (section 12 row 1, section 14, table 14.1): 'test/e2e/kit/stand.js: reads TEMP'. Cause: stand.js reads the base list of C-1 by name (decision 0109 О10), and six of its names (TEMP, TMP, LANG, LC_ALL, TZ, SystemRoot) are not in the list ENV_NAMES of the test. New expected behaviour: ENV_NAMES gets those six names (PATH and TMPDIR are in it already); the rules 'no whole-environment read outside find-chrome.js, browser.js, runner.js', 'no computed key outside cleanup.js' and 'NODE_TEST_CONTEXT only in runner.js' stay. Fixed by TEST-DESIGNER at sub-step 3; left red here. Evidence: S1 on a fresh clone of the tag (52/51/1), S2 in the project (52/51/1), the full suite (2187/2186/1, the only failure E2K-50). No other test is red.

The draft. The four files of the write set existed before this run (left by the run that the owner's pause stopped; stand.js 427 lines, fake-stand.js 163 lines, mode 0755, the export line, the README edits). They were not taken as done work: each was compared with the design (the options and rules of 4.1, the seven steps of startStand, the members of Stand, stop() and its precedence, withStand, the codes and the message shapes, section 5 rows 1-12, section 6, the events and modes of 4.3, section 10) and run (checks (a), (b), the trial). Changed: one message of stand.js (CLEANUP_FAILED when the main process did not end). Kept: everything else.

For CODE-DESIGNER through ORCH (not a departure; the code follows the rule as written). Section 4.1, stop(): 'Only when the group is gone: if the exit was not code 0 with no signal -> STAND_EXIT …', and then 'A process that ended by itself before stop() is cleaned up the same way and stop() then throws STAND_EXIT (a crashed server fails the test that used it)'. Both give the same result for a crashed server (a code other than 0 or a signal; die-later: 'exit code 5 on its own', shown). They differ for a server that ended by itself with exit code 0 before stop(): by the rule (and C-3, the README 'requires the exit code 0') stop() resolves {code: 0, signal: null}; by a literal reading of the second sentence it would throw STAND_EXIT '… exit code 0 on its own'. stand.js follows the rule. No test of 11.1 covers this case. If the second reading is wanted, it is a one-condition change of stop() and one more test for TEST-DESIGNER; ORCH decides.

Option checks beyond those that section 5 row 1 names (name, args, pattern, env value). The code (from the draft, kept) also refuses with USAGE, in step 1, before anything is made or spawned: options that are not an object; env that is not an object; an env name that is not a variable name; a NUL in an env value (as for args; otherwise spawn would throw after the marker is made); a cwd that is not a non-empty string without NUL (a cwd that does not exist still goes to spawn and gives STAND_START_FAILED, E2S-04); stateDirs that is not a list; a timeout that is not a whole number above 0; a deps.spawn that is not a function; and in withStand a body that is not a function (as withBrowser). They are checks of the options of the 4.1 table on the path of step 1; no design test depends on them; REVIEWER may judge them.

A wait that the design does not name. When the process ends, the starter waits for the close of its pipes at most 1000 ms before it takes the last stderr line for STAND_START_EXITED and STAND_EXIT (the exit event can come before the last bytes are read; browser.js does the same with 300 ms). It is a wait for a fact with a limit, its timer is cleared on close; stop() resolves only after the close, so stdout() and stderr() are complete then (E2S-12). No fixed sleep stands in stand.js; in fake-stand.js the only delays are those of the 4.3 contract (ok-late 800 ms, die-later 300 ms) and the 5 ms back-off on EAGAIN of the released kit pattern (fake-chrome.js, runner.js).

Gate remarks N18-N20 (step 01f). N18: the SIGTERM handler of the --child process appends {event: 'child-term', pid}; check (b) shows that a SIGTERM to the child pid and the group SIGTERM of stop() both write it, and that the child stays alive until SIGKILL. The assertion in E2S-13 that would catch the mutant S19 is TEST-DESIGNER's (sub-step 3). N19: a synchronous throw of spawn gives STAND_START_FAILED with the marker removed and nothing registered (shown by the own trial); its test is TEST-DESIGNER's. N20: STAND_EXIT says ' after SIGTERM' when stop() sent the signal ('fake ended with exit code 1 after SIGTERM. …', shown); its assertion is TEST-DESIGNER's.

Beyond 4.3 in the stand-in (from the draft, kept): an unknown SAI_FAKE_STAND_MODE writes 'fake stand: unknown mode <mode>' to stderr and exits 2 after the start and env events, so a misspelt mode in a test fails at once (STAND_START_EXITED) instead of running as ok. A mode that TEST-DESIGNER adds (4.3 allows it) must also be added to the set MODES of the file.
